opportunities.title: Quality, conduct and safety assurance
opportunities.customer_problem: Inconsistent skill, incomplete work, damaged property, rude or unsafe conduct, rating pressure and doubts about honesty.
opportunities.supporting_segment: Salon and massage (safety), AC and appliance repair (damage)
opportunities.expected_customer_benefit: Consistent work and a sense of safety, especially for people alone at home.
opportunities.influence_on_repeat_booking_hypothesis: Customers who say they will return mostly praise the individual professional. Making that quality consistent, and making it easy to rebook the good one, should convert more first bookings into repeat bookings (hypothesis).
opportunities.suggested_improvement_hypothesis: (1) Skill-matched assignment: Match professionals to jobs by verified skill and past results, with refreshers where quality slips. (2) Proof of work: A short checklist and before/after photos the customer approves before the job closes. (3) Damage cover that works: Visible cover with a fast claim path and a stated settlement time. (4) Safety by design: Verified identity, shareable job status, a female-professional option, and ratings and tips requested in the app, not in person.
opportunities.suggested_success_metric: A higher share of jobs rated well without a complaint, faster damage settlement, fewer safety complaints, and more rebooking of the same professional.

why_it_happens_hypotheses: Assignment is not matched to skill and category experience.
There is no customer-visible proof of completed work.
Damage claims are slow, and in-person rating requests create pressure.

opportunities.title: Arrival guarantee and proactive recovery
opportunities.customer_problem: A confirmed booking is cancelled, rescheduled, late or never attended, and customers are charged or left without a replacement.
opportunities.expected_customer_benefit: Customers can plan around the slot; fewer wasted days and fewer fees for failures that are not theirs.
opportunities.influence_on_repeat_booking_hypothesis: A failed first booking is the earliest and cheapest point to lose a customer. A fast, visible recovery turns a failure into a reason to trust the platform, which should raise the chance of a second booking (hypothesis: compare 90-day repeat for first bookings that were late or cancelled and recovered vs not recovered).
opportunities.suggested_improvement_hypothesis: (1) Confirm before you charge: Show the named professional and arrival window at confirmation; treat a booking as confirmed only when a professional has accepted. (2) Two-way confirmation and live ETA: Professional confirms the morning of the job; the customer sees live status and gets a proactive alert on any delay (a customer asked for exactly this). (3) Automatic recovery: If a professional cancels or is late beyond a threshold, auto-offer the next available professional or a priority reschedule, plus a goodwill credit that applies to the next booking. (4) No customer penalty for provider failure: Waive every fee when the cancellation is not the customer's; add reliability to professional scoring and assignment.
opportunities.suggested_success_metric: More bookings fulfilled on the first scheduled slot, faster replacement after a provider cancellation, and a smaller repeat-rate gap between customers whose first booking failed and those whose first booking went well.

opportunities.title: Human-reachable support with first-contact resolution
opportunities.customer_problem: Customers cannot reach a person, bots repeat templates, tickets are closed unresolved, and nobody owns the problem.
opportunities.expected_customer_benefit: A problem becomes a short, owned conversation instead of a stalemate.
opportunities.influence_on_repeat_booking_hypothesis: The experience of getting a problem fixed seems to decide whether customers stay, more than the original failure itself. Fast, human resolution should keep customers who would otherwise leave after a single failure (hypothesis: compare repeat rate of customers who complained and were resolved at first contact vs those who were not).
opportunities.suggested_improvement_hypothesis: (1) A person on request: After one bot exchange, or at once for a paid booking issue, offer a callback within a stated time. Show the phone or chat option in the booking screen. (2) One case, one owner: A single case ID with a named owner, visible status and deadline in the app; a case closes only when the customer confirms or a clear resolution is recorded. (3) Empowered first contact: Let first-line agents approve refunds, redos and goodwill credits up to a cap so most problems end in one contact. (4) Reach out first: After a cancelled, late or very low-rated job, contact the customer proactively before they complain, and check back after resolution.
opportunities.suggested_success_metric: Customers reach a human quickly, most complaints end in one contact, few cases are reopened, and customers who complained rebook at a rate close to those who did not.

opportunities.title: All-in price lock and on-site upsell guardrails
opportunities.customer_problem: Prices change between quote, app and bill; stacked fees on small jobs; parts or extra work quoted on site at much higher rates than local providers.
opportunities.expected_customer_benefit: Predictable total cost and confidence that the on-site quote is fair.
opportunities.influence_on_repeat_booking_hypothesis: Price surprises damage trust, and customers who feel overcharged compare with local providers. A predictable bill makes the next booking a known quantity (hypothesis: repeat rate of customers whose final bill matched the quote vs those whose bill rose).
opportunities.suggested_improvement_hypothesis: (1) One all-in price, locked: Show the full price including fees and taxes before payment and honour it; if it changes, explain why in one line. (2) In-app approval for extras: Any additional part or work is quoted in the app with a price cap, and the customer approves it before work starts. (3) Public rate card for common parts: Publish typical prices so customers can see an upsell is not out of line with local rates. (4) Small-job pricing: Review fee structure for small jobs, where fees weigh most and customers compare with local providers.
opportunities.suggested_success_metric: The final bill matches the booked price for almost every job, extras are approved in the app, and price complaints fall, particularly for small-ticket repeat categories.

opportunities.title: One-tap rework and Native after-sales
opportunities.customer_problem: Warranty is refused or expires in days, rework needs repeated requests, and Native purifier installation or service is delayed or unsupported.
opportunities.supporting_segment: Water Purifier / RO and AC Service & Repair
opportunities.expected_customer_benefit: Work that fails after the visit is fixed without a fight.
opportunities.influence_on_repeat_booking_hypothesis: A repair that fails soon after is a strong reason to switch providers, and Native owners are long-term customers by design. Fixing it without a fight should protect the next booking (hypothesis).
opportunities.suggested_improvement_hypothesis: (1) One-tap 'problem after service': Inside the warranty window, one tap reschedules the same or another professional within a stated time. (2) Warranty visible per job: Show what is covered and the end date on the booking, and consider longer cover on high-value repairs. (3) Native after-sales tracker: Installation and service status with a promised date, a dedicated support line and proactive delay updates. (4) Hand-off when out of scope: If a fault is outside the service, say so plainly and point to the brand or a recommended option instead of leaving the customer stranded.
opportunities.suggested_success_metric: Rework requests are completed quickly, warranty disputes fall, Native installations meet the promised date, and customers who needed rework still rebook.

opportunities.title: Instant refunds and payment-failure recovery
opportunities.customer_problem: Money is deducted without a booking, refunds are slow or partial, and customers who paid in advance feel they cannot get it back.
opportunities.expected_customer_benefit: Customers regain money and trust quickly; less resentment of advance payment.
opportunities.influence_on_repeat_booking_hypothesis: A refund that takes weeks turns a one-off failure into a grievance about paying in the app at all. Instant, visible refunds should remove a common reason for not coming back (hypothesis).
opportunities.suggested_improvement_hypothesis: (1) Automatic refund to source: Refund automatically, with a visible tracker and expected date, whenever the company or professional cancels or a payment succeeds without a booking. (2) Instant credit option: Offer an immediate in-app credit as an alternative to a 5-7 day bank refund, so the customer can rebook straight away. (3) Reconcile within minutes: If money is taken and no booking exists, create the booking or reverse the charge automatically and tell the customer. (4) Pay after service for small jobs: Test pay-after-service for low-value jobs, which several customers asked for.
opportunities.suggested_success_metric: Refunds reach the customer in hours instead of weeks, almost no case is stuck in 'paid but not booked', and customers who received a refund rebook at a normal rate.

opportunities.title: Flexible small-job and add-on packages
opportunities.customer_problem: Minimum-order rules, no single-bathroom or per-task option, no way to extend time, and requests for services that do not exist.
opportunities.expected_customer_benefit: Pay for exactly the job needed and get small jobs done without a minimum order.
opportunities.influence_on_repeat_booking_hypothesis: Small jobs are where customers turn to local providers. Serving them should keep customers booking between larger jobs (hypothesis).
opportunities.suggested_improvement_hypothesis: (1) Per-task and single-unit options: Single-bathroom cleaning and similar small units with clear scope. (2) Add-on and time extension: Let the customer extend the visit or add a task in the app, at a stated price. (3) Capture missing demand: A custom request form that records requested services, and test the most requested categories.
opportunities.suggested_success_metric: Fewer abandoned carts at the minimum-order step, more small-job bookings, and a repeat rate for small-job customers closer to the average.

opportunities.expected_customer_benefit: Reliable quality from someone they trust, without paying extra to rebook.
opportunities.influence_on_repeat_booking_hypothesis: Several customers say outright they will call the same professional again. Making that one tap should convert a good job directly into a repeat booking (hypothesis; the most direct link to the metric).
opportunities.suggested_improvement_hypothesis: (1) Book again with the same professional: A prominent action on the completion screen and in booking history, at no extra charge. (2) Honour dislikes: After a complaint, never reassign that professional to that customer. (3) Suggest favourites: Recommend the customer's well-rated professionals for the next category they need.
opportunities.suggested_success_metric: More bookings rebooked with the same professional, and a higher 90-day repeat rate after a five-star job when the rebook prompt is shown.

opportunities.title: Coverage waitlist and tier-2/3 expansion
opportunities.customer_problem: Customers in unserved areas and cities cannot book at all; some download the app and find nothing.
opportunities.expected_customer_benefit: Access to the service, or a clear date when it will arrive.
opportunities.influence_on_repeat_booking_hypothesis: Customers who cannot book cannot return. A waitlist keeps the relationship alive until service arrives (hypothesis; the evidence here is thin).
opportunities.suggested_improvement_hypothesis: (1) Pincode waitlist: Let customers join a waitlist by pincode and see nearby available categories. (2) Use demand to decide expansion: Rank areas by waitlist demand to prioritise partner onboarding.
opportunities.suggested_success_metric: Waitlist sign-ups by pincode, and bookings from waitlisted customers soon after launch.

prioritisation.formula: 0.25*frequency(share of dataset/15%, cap 1) + 0.20*severity(share Negative) + 0.20*evidence(source breadth and volume) + 0.20*repeat relevance(4 x share with non-return/switching/warning, cap 1) + 0.15*impact(analyst judgement 1-5, a hypothesis)

opportunities.priority_rationale: Affects 53 reviews (2.1% of the dataset), 32.1% Negative, present in 2 of 4 sources; 9.4% of these reviews contain switching, warning or non-return signals (dataset baseline 12.3%).

pm_brief.problem: In some areas and smaller cities customers open the app and find no service, or a category that is unavailable, with no sign of when it will arrive.
pm_brief.who_is_affected: Customers in unserved pincodes and tier-2/3 cities.
why_it_happens_hypotheses: Supply has not been built in low-density areas.
Customers who cannot book leave no record of their demand.

proposal.title: Pincode waitlist
proposal.what: Let customers join a waitlist by pincode and see nearby available categories.

proposal.title: Use demand to decide expansion
proposal.what: Rank areas by waitlist demand to prioritise partner onboarding.

pm_brief.why_it_should_lift_repeat_booking: Customers who cannot book cannot return. A waitlist keeps the relationship alive until service arrives (hypothesis; the evidence here is thin).
pm_brief.success_looks_like: Waitlist sign-ups by pincode, and bookings from waitlisted customers soon after launch.
pm_brief.watch_outs: A waitlist raises expectations; communicate timelines honestly.
pm_brief.effort_note: Small build; the expansion itself is a business decision.
pm_brief.labels: Customer evidence (counts, quotes) comes from the reviews. Root causes, proposals, the repeat-booking mechanism and effort are product-manager hypotheses and judgements, not findings.

distinction: 'evidence' fields are customer-reported and computed from the dataset; fields ending in _hypothesis, the impact judgement and the success metrics are product hypotheses and recommendations, not findings.
